rows.subject: How long a person has to bring an employment tribunal claim
rows.today: the primary limit is worked out from the date it runs from: for a relevant date before 1 October 2026 three months, on or after it six (Schedule 12 to the Employment Rights Act 2025, with regulation 4 of S.I. 2026/954), each from the words of the provision as it stood for that date, read from its publisher when asked, with who to ask; early conciliation and extensions are not accounted for, and breach of contract claims are worked out for England and Wales and for Scotland, each either side of its own change: six months from 1 October 2026 (S.I. 2026/759) and from 9 November 2026 (S.S.I. 2026/327), the Scottish one read with the change its publisher lists as not yet written into its text; and a claim no rule here is for, or one whose rule is not for the nation asked about, is answered that a time limit may still apply, with where to ask today for that nation (built in W875; dated either side of the change in W1157; breach of contract added in W1160; the answer with no rule, nation by nation, in W1161; each rule's sources, read when and by whom and said as not recently checked ninety days on, and a month with no such day worked out to the earlier of the two days it could end on with the sentence that the provision does not settle it, in W1162)

rows.subject: How long a person has to bring an employment tribunal claim in Northern Ireland

rows.subject: A document whose preparation is a reserved instrument activity: an instrument of transfer or charge of land, an instrument for land registration, a contract for the sale or other disposition of land beyond a short lease, a deed for registration
rows.today: the draft form drafts only the templates it lists, and refuses any other id before anything is composed (W1194); the words of a listed template's request - each party label and value, its instructions and its jurisdiction - are read for an explicit ask to prepare one of the reserved documents, in the words the screen knows (a drafting verb, I need, can you, please or the document is, asking for the form TR1, TP1, AS1, CH1, AP1 or FR1, a transfer deed or a transfer of a house, a flat or land, a legal charge or a mortgage deed, a contract for the sale of land, or a lease of land for more than three years), and the template id the clerk is given for the document it names; a request or an id it reads so is refused before anything is composed or stored, saying what the screen read, where, and what it took it as asking for (W1195); the clerk holds a template id that names a deed, as the draft form does (held since W714); each refusal says the reserved documents (read from the register of sources' row lsa-2007-sch2 by this platform, not by a qualified person, with the day it was read and what it did not read) and where help is, the fabric's form meets the same refusal, and the Law page says them beside the held deed; a mention with no ask word is not refused, but a request about one of the documents phrased as an ask ('I need my TR1 checked') can be, and the screen misses most other ways of asking: a draft request it does not read is drafted, and its answer says the screen read no ask, which is not a clearance, and a template id the clerk is given that it does not read is assembled and stored, and that answer says nothing of the screen. Measured on 2026-11-22: on the red team's 120 blind cases the word screen this replaced recognised 7 of 50 reserved asks and refused 2 of 70 ordinary drafts and 16 of 20 property-sector ones. This screen's own figures are in-sample, the cases seen while it was written: through the draft form it refuses 1 of the red team's 50 and none of the 70 or the 20, 10 of the 50 are refused before it reads them (an unlisted id, or a held or filing-shaped template) and 39 are drafted; on the corpus written for this round, which it was fixed against, it recognises 27 of 87 reserved asks and refuses none of 116 ordinary ones; on its labelled list it reads 33 of 164 asks and refuses none of 168 others. Out of sample, the final check's 80 ordinary drafts and 15 explicit asks, written before it read the screen and not used to fix it: none of the 80 refused, all 15 read; its 15 drafts written near the screen's patterns (5 were refused) and the requests about a document it named led to the last fixes and are labelled now, so precision on unseen requests near the patterns is not measured (FU-1891's blind set is where it will be); the same screen reads the words of a request to the Generator's POST /api/v1/generator/produce (its specification, artefact type, format and domain, each on its own and together), the Synthesis Studio's POST /api/v1/synthesis/generate and /stream (its instructions, after the ruling check and before a stream starts; not its files), POST /api/v1/refine (the instruction to refine a tool's output, the Law page's draft among them, and the title it is given; not the draft) and a fabric composition's run (its objective, or with none its name, its usage area, and each resource's settings and their names, before any stage is built), and refuses an ask it reads there with 409 before anything is composed or saved, each refusal naming its route and saying that the screen misses most other ways of asking; the fabric's Generator stage, called in process, says the Generator's refusal as a refusal; a reserved document named as another document's subject ('a TR1 explainer', 'a lesson on a legal charge') is not read as asked for (W1195b, at its legal review); the screen is otherwise W1195's, with its limits, so a request it does not read there is composed, which is not a clearance. Measured at those doors on 2026-11-27: none of the builder's own 72 ordinary requests or requests about a document, written for those doors before the screen was run on them (out of sample, but not blind), was refused, nor any of the legal review's 30 ordinary requests the screen refused before that change (labelled after it, so in-sample); 17 of the builder's 19 explicit asks were read, a figure that is high because the builder had read the screen's patterns, while the recall that generalises is W1195's (27 of 87 on its corpus, in-sample; 1 of 50 on the red team's cases, their fields read together); the platform's other free-text generators are not screened, among them the deliverables, the Application Studio, the Creator Studio, the Factory, the in-house assistant, the avatar, the AI CEO's chat and support (W1194, W1195, W1195b)

rows.subject: Keeping a record of the enterprise's own agreement with an outside party
rows.nation: Any: the record states no rule of law
rows.today: on the Law page, a signed-in person enters each party as a person or a registered body with where and when it was read, drafts an agreement on those party records only, and records its review, the approval of one exact version, its execution as their own entry of the evidence and the formalities met, that it is in force and its end, each with who and when; a change to the text ends the approval it had; nothing is kept before sign-in, which formalities the law requires is not stated, and nothing here is legal advice (built in W1080 and W1081)

rows.subject: Keeping the evidence for a physical asset held under the enterprise's agreement
rows.nation: Any: the record states no rule of law
rows.today: on the Law page, a signed-in person enters a vehicle, robot, drone or instrument as a record owned and possessed by party records and held under an agreement record, and attaches evidence to its six facts apart - the right to use it, the place's permission, the maker's conformity, their own safety evidence, insurance and a named person's declaration of readiness - each with who, when and when it lapses; evidence past its date reads lapsed and a declaration resting on it withdrawn; no score or word of readiness is computed, nothing is connected or controlled, and nothing is kept before sign-in (built in W1082 and W1083)

rows.subject: Which rules apply where a physical asset would be used, as sources
rows.nation: Great Britain and the UK, as each row of the register of sources says
rows.today: on the Law page, a signed-in person says where an asset would be used - in a workplace, on a road, on a public footway, in the air or somewhere else - and is shown the rows of the register of sources for that use, each with what it says, the date it was read, by whom and what was not read; where no source permitting the use was found, the record says so in those words; nothing says whether the law permits the use (built in W1084)

rows.subject: What the enterprise's agreement obliges, and when, and what waits on a person
rows.nation: Any: the record states no rule of law
